clue.text: Space ill-used to produce Jamaican pepper

indicators.note: with 'ill' before it, used reads as ill-used, badly treated, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as part of the fodder
taken as written as the rest of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone wastes the room they have when making a spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-used' looks like a single adjective, but ILL is part of the fodder and 'used' alone signals the anagram of SPACE plus ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Allspice is the dried berry of a Caribbean tree, also called pimento or Jamaica pepper.

clue.text: He also called Ulysses a hero

definitions.text: He also called Ulysses a hero

parts.words: He also called Ulysses a hero
parts.note: the Greek hero of Homer's epic was known to the Romans under the Latin name Ulysses, the title of Joyce's novel

explanation.definitionFit: The Homeric king of Ithaca is the same figure Latin writers named Ulysses.

clue.text: Awkward dive onto the net, struggling to get clear

indicators.note: awkward means clumsy and out of shape, so the word dive is rearranged
struggling suggests thrashing about, so the word net is jumbled too

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper dives clumsily onto the net, fighting to clear the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' turns DIVE into EVID and 'struggling' turns NET into ENT; 'onto the' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evident is plain to see, as obvious as a clear fact.

clue.text: A mistake to take backward students

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the word for students from its end to its start

parts.note: students are pupils

explanation.surface: It would be an error to accept slow learners.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip-up is a careless error or blunder.

clue.text: Old leper-house built on London fields

definitions.text: Old leper-house built on London fields

parts.words: Old leper-house built on London fields
parts.note: an archaic word for a ... for lepers, which gave its name to an area of East London named after the fields it stood in

explanation.walkthrough: Spitalfields in East London takes its name from a medieval hospital, St Mary Spital.
explanation.definitionFit: Spital is an obsolete term for a hospital, especially one for lepers or the poor.

clue.text: At every spa, it's rightly formed

definitions.text: At every spa, it's rightly formed

parts.words: At every spa, it's rightly formed
parts.note: a spa is a well, and every such place is developed for visitors; read straight, the phrase means properly shaped

explanation.definitionFit: Something properly grown or shaped with full proportions is described as fully matured and soundly built.

clue.text: Untamed, like the bison?

definitions.meaning: untamed means rough, lawless and uncivilised
the bison is a wild animal with a shaggy coat, literally a beast both feral and fleecy

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for rough and lawless, and literally fits a feral, shaggy-coated bison.

clue.text: Complete break — relative can go to the devil!

indicators.note: can go to says the word for a relative is placed after the devil's name

parts.note: Dis is the god of the underworld in Roman myth, a name for the devil
a relative is a connection by family

explanation.surface: Someone cuts off all contact, telling a family member to go to hell.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete severance of links or contact is a total split.

clue.text: Finishes, despite time lost on cupboards

indicators.note: lost signals that the letter for time goes missing from the word for cupboards

parts.note: closets are cupboards

explanation.surface: Someone finishes the job even though time has been wasted on the cupboards.
explanation.definitionFit: To finish something is to bring it to an end, as a shop shuts for the day.

clue.text: Stand in when pet is due to be operated on

indicators.note: something operated on is cut open and worked over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A vet's locum takes over when an animal is booked for surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: To deputise is to act as a substitute for someone else.

clue.text: Perceive where the bishop's responsibility lies

definitions.meaning: to perceive is to notice or observe
a bishop's diocese, the area under his authority

explanation.definitionFit: The word means to notice, and is also the ecclesiastical term for a bishop's jurisdiction.

clue.text: Spite shown by little beasts around Albania

indicators.note: around means the little beasts wrap round the abbreviation for Albania

parts.note: mice are small creatures
AL is Albania's international vehicle registration code

explanation.surface: Small creatures behaving spitefully near Albania.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite and ill will are synonyms for a wish to harm others.

clue.text: Pole? No, another Corsican with big ideas!

definitions.text: Pole? No, another Corsican with big ideas!

parts.words: Pole? No, another Corsican with big ideas!
parts.note: the ambitious emperor born in Corsica, whose name opens with letters that echo 'Pole' and 'No'

explanation.walkthrough: The letters of POLE and NO appear within the name, but no indicator turns them into it, so the clue reads as a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: The French emperor born in Ajaccio was famous for vast imperial ambitions.

clue.text: African chief who'd love an academic qualification

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, written as O
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A tribal leader who would like a university degree.
explanation.definitionFit: An oba is a hereditary ruler among the Yoruba and Edo peoples of Nigeria.

clue.text: Disinclined to take daughter in? The contrary!

indicators.note: take, with the later 'in', says the word for disinclined holds the letter for daughter
in completes the instruction to put the daughter inside

parts.note: averse means unwilling or disinclined

explanation.surface: Is someone unwilling to take their daughter in? Quite the opposite!
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means opposing or hostile, acting against.

clue.text: Gypsy gentleman found in Peckham

definitions.meaning: in Romany, a ... is a gentleman, as in Borrow's 'Romany ...'
Peckham ... is a common and district of South London

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the Romany term for a gentleman and part of the South London place name Peckham Rye.

clue.text: Irritating dish, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: rubbing so as to make sore
a ... dish is a warming pan for food at table, so the word can describe a dish

explanation.definitionFit: The word means rubbing sore, and names a pan used to keep food warm.

clue.text: Periods given wholly, from the sound of it, to sacred rites

definitions.text: Periods given wholly, from the sound of it, to sacred rites

indicators.note: from the sound of it says the word wholly is heard rather than read

parts.note: said aloud, wholly sounds like a word meaning sacred
days are periods of time

explanation.surface: Times devoted entirely to religious ceremonies.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also describes the answer: days given wholly to worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious festivals are days set aside for worship and observance.

clue.text: For some, you add, it was durrell's alexandrian books

indicators.note: add tells us to slip the letter for you into the phrase before it

parts.note: U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: To some readers, you'd add, Durrell's Alexandria novels were this.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence Durrell's Alexandria Quartet is four novels, so a set of four.
explanation.definitionFit: Durrell's Alexandria Quartet comprises four novels, a group of four.

clue.text: When at home, is apt to make plans

parts.note: in means at home
tends means is apt or inclined to

explanation.surface: When staying in, someone is inclined to make plans.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan something is to mean or aim to do it.

clue.text: Centaur?

parts.note: the half-man, half-horse of Greek myth is literally a man who is part horse

explanation.definitionFit: A rider on horseback, of which the mythical creature is a whimsical fused version.

clue.text: The most rational and sensible way

parts.note: sane means sensible
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: The most reasonable and sensible approach.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of the soundest mind is to be most reasonable.

clue.text: Spark that's creative

parts.note: a spark of creativity on the surface, but really the Scottish novelist Spark, author of 'The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie'

explanation.definitionFit: The forename of the writer Dame Spark, author of 'The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie'.

clue.text: Dine aboard ship

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Dine aboard ship' (LAUNCH): LUNCH with A inside, where the single word 'aboard' gives the A and is also the container indicator, a word doing two jobs

clue.text: Flower stays concealed

indicators.note: concealed means the river is tucked away within the word stays

explanation.definitionFit: A flower is crossword-speak for a river, a thing that flows; the Tay is Scotland's longest.

clue.text: Curiously, one lord's some kind of Norwegian

indicators.note: curiously means oddly, so the letters are mixed into a strange new order

parts.note: taken with its S as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Oddly, a certain nobleman is a kind of Norwegian.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval language of Scandinavia is the ancestor of Norwegian.

clue.text: Make whisky in a day — it's bad, I'll throw away a litre

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day

indicators.note: bad suggests the word it's goes wrong and is jumbled
throw away says one litre symbol is removed from I'll

parts.note: the word I'll written without its apostrophe
L is the symbol for litre

explanation.surface: A distiller complains a day's whisky-making has gone bad and a litre must be discarded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' turns ITS into IST; 'throw away' drops one L from ILL to leave IL.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisky is made by distillation of fermented grain mash.

clue.text: He ran out of time this morning

definitions.text: He ran out of time this morning

parts.words: He ran out of time this morning
parts.note: someone whose day is done before noon is a has-been, his time belonging to the day before

explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a person, especially a politician, whose influence is past.
